_comment: ZERO SUM — WORLD AND OBJECTS generation group.
Authority: docs/ART_UPGRADE_PLAN.md (tiers §2, generation §3, bake §4) and
docs/VISUAL_REDESIGN.md §3.1 / §3.3 / §3.4 / §3.5 / §3.6 / Part 7 / Appendix A.
Targets are emitted WIRE PIXELS AT RS=4: TilePxR=24, WorldPxR=1152.
== WHAT IS IN THIS GROUP ==
12 entries, 19 API calls, 27 source cells.
Tier A: rock clusters (2x2, 3x2, orphan), pedestal (armed/disarmed), bush clump,
item chip body, pod crate body, 12 contents stencils, burst star.
Tier B: floor field (1152x1152), wall / Fortress roof face (384x384 seamless).
== CROSS-GROUP: THE SIX WEAPON GLYPHS ARE NOT HERE, AND THAT NEEDS A DECISION ==
The plan lists weapon glyphs (sword/spear/bow/knives/blowgun/net, 20x20, SpWeaponBase
601..606) in Tier A. They are authored in prompts/characters.json as `weapon-glyphs`,
because the glyph is drawn at the living carrier's hand point and is therefore PHOSPHOR —
live signal on a living agent — not amber matter. That is the right home and this file
does not duplicate the entry: two entries would bill two calls and produce two conflicting
cuts of the same six sprite ids.
But it leaves ONE VOCABULARY SPLIT ACROSS TWO GENERATIONS, which is exactly the drift the
sheet strategy exists to prevent. Sword, spear, bow, knives, blowgun and net each appear
TWICE in this build: as a contents mark on the amber chip and the amber crate (cells 1-6 of
stencil-sheet here) and as the held glyph in an agent's hand (characters/weapon-glyphs).
If those two drawings disagree, a player has to learn each weapon twice. They currently DO
disagree by design: characters puts all six on one shared 45-degree diagonal and separates
sword from spear by width, length and a crossbar; stencil-sheet separates sword (vertical),
spear (diagonal) and blowgun (horizontal) by AXIS, on the argument that axis is the only
difference that survives a 16x reduction. Both are defensible; they cannot both ship.
Resolution to take before generating either sheet — the cheapest option is also the
strongest: drop characters/weapon-glyphs entirely and cut the held glyphs as a CONCENTRIC
SECOND CROP of stencil-sheet cells 1-6 — 320x320 instead of 384x384, same centre, k=4 at
16x -> 20x20 — tinted phosphor in code from the same alpha mask. Zero extra images, zero
drift, and the sword a player learns on a ground chip is pixel-identical to the sword in an
enemy's hand. Cost: the mark lands at 14 of 20 px (70% fill) because the stencil marks are
sized for a 24px canvas, against 16 of 20 px (80%) for a dedicated 20px cut. If the re-crop
reads too light at 1:1 on the poster, keep characters/weapon-glyphs but re-author its six
descriptions to match stencil-sheet cells 1-6 word for word.
== WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT IN THIS GROUP ==
parachute (podChutePixels) — RETIRED by the bible: 'the machine prints deliveries, it
does not parachute them'. SpPodChute is dead art (defined in every init packet, never
placed). Plan §2 Tier C: DELETE, do not regenerate. The pod crate's row-by-row print
reveal (cratePartPixels) replaces it, and is a row-slice of the baked crate below.
projectiles (projPixels) — Tier C. They need 4-8 ROTATIONS (today's trail is always
horizontal regardless of heading, render.nim:1605). Rotation is one line of math versus
eight mutually-consistent hand-prompted images. Phase 1 re-authors them natively at
TilePxR with native=true; their colour comes from the Phase-2 amber itemColor collapse.
backgroundPixels — the compositor itself. 0 images, forever: it is a runtime function of
the PRNG-seeded rock layout (30-44 rock tiles at different coords per seed), the
shrinking safe radius and the de-rez level.
plasma / ring ghost / flood / storm / halos / reticle / trace / all text — Tier C
(analytic circles, dithered two-parity fields, live strings). See plan §2.
carrier hull, corpse wreck, and the three body-derived overlays (camo glass, camo-reveal
glitch, hit flash) plus the 8-frame death decomposition — the CHARACTER group. The three
overlays and the death frames are 0 images by construction: they are derived at BAKE TIME
from the baked carrier's alpha mask, because generating them independently guarantees
misregistration (plan §2 Tier B, risk #3).
== CROP GEOMETRY (plan §3.3 hard rule: crop.w/target.w == crop.h/target.h == 2^k, k>=2) ==
entry                 frame (est)     crop            k        target
stencil-sheet         2048x1536       12 x 384x384    4 (16x)  24x24 each (cells 512x512)
(held weapon glyphs, if cut from stencil-sheet: 12 x 320x320, k=4 (16x) -> 20x20, same
cell centres as the 384x384 stencil crops — concentric, so both rects are verified once.)
Frame sizes are ESTIMATES. generate.py measures the real PNG and records actual_px in
art/raw/world/_manifest.json — cut every rect in art/sheets.json against actual_px, by eye,
once. Segmentation is manifest-declared and hand-verified; a mis-crop is silent (§3.3).
== FRAMING CONVENTION ==
Every keyed entry states its own framing as a fraction of the frame, so the hand-cut rect
is the subject and the subject fills its final canvas. 'middle three quarters' == the
1536x1536 crop of a 2048 frame; 'a little more than half' == the 1152 crop. Do not read
these as safety margin: a subject drawn smaller than stated wastes final pixels (a rock
drawn at half the frame lands as a 12px blob in a 24px tile).
== OVERRIDES OF THE SHARED PREFIX (deliberate, not oversight) ==
prompt_prefix/prompt_suffix carry the AFTERGLOW constraint block from plan §3.2 VERBATIM
and byte-identical to every other group's file — that block is the palette law and the
chroma-key law and it must never drift. Two clauses in it are carrier-class defaults that
world entries restate:
1. 'Orthographic front view' — board props are seen from directly above (floor tiles,
pedestals, chips) or from above and slightly in front (rocks, bushes, crates), which is
the viewpoint the renderer already draws (rockAt's up-left key, podCratePixels' lit top
face). Each entry restates its own viewpoint in its first sentence; the body follows the
prefix in the joined prompt, so the later, more specific statement wins.
2. 'Background: flat pure #00FF00' and 'Single key light from the upper left' — WRONG for
the two Tier B materials, which have no background (they are full-bleed fields) and must
have no light direction at all (a lit gradient is a vignette, and a vignette is what makes
a tile repeat and a mosaic seam visible). floor-field and wall-face open with an explicit
MATERIAL SWATCH override paragraph. All lighting on those two is applied by the renderer:
plateAt's per-tile shade hash and panel joints, parapetColorAt's 4-ray bevel classification.
== VERIFIED FACTS ABOUT THE PIPELINE ON THESE PALETTES ==
Checked numerically against all 39 tokens of the §3.5 ramps + semantics + team wheel:
- The despill step (g = min(g, max(r,b)+12), plan §3.4 step 3) is a provable NO-OP on every
legal colour: g <= max(r,b)+12 holds for all 39. It can be applied unconditionally, with no
special case for the two full-bleed material sheets.
- The key detector (g>190 && r<110 && b<110, step 2) has zero false positives on legal colours.
- No legal token lands in hue 75..165 deg. The nearest is Phosphor #A5E3EE / #8ACFDC at ~189
deg, i.e. 24 deg of margin. So the palette lint's green-hue reject band should be 75..165
deg at saturation > 8% (risk #6). Nothing in AFTERGLOW can trip it; only model spill can.
== TRAPS ==
- DO NOT put `seed` in defaults. `variants: N` sends the SAME request body N times; a fixed
seed would return N identical images and silently collapse the 3 rock draws and the 4 floor
quadrants into one repeated picture — the exact failure the mosaic exists to avoid.
- Sheets are ONE call. Never split a sheet into per-cell calls to fix one bad cell without
reading the sheet-vs-single comment on that entry first.
- `notes` is carried into _manifest.json (baker-facing). `comment` is ignored by generate.py
and exists for the human reading this file (design rationale). Neither is sent to the API.
- Crop rects live in art/sheets.json, never here (README + plan §3.3).

defaults.prompt_prefix:
Orthographic front view, straight on, no perspective, no camera tilt.
Single key light from the upper left. No cast shadow (the shadow is drawn separately).
Background: flat pure #00FF00, edge to edge. There must be no other green anywhere.
No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark, no signature.
defaults.prompt_suffix:
The subject will be composited onto a dark slate ground, RGB(40,48,57) — light it for that.

Palette, strictly:
  structure / stone / chassis  -> desaturated blue-grey, #1C242B to #4E5E6B only
  living signal / emission     -> pale cyan phosphor #A5E3EE, highlights to #EAF7FA
  matter, loot, money, energy  -> warm amber #FFB454
  contact shadow / ink line    -> near-black blue #10161C
Nothing warm except the amber. Nothing green. Nothing saturated red unless asked.

prompts.name: floor-field
prompts.prompt:
MATERIAL SWATCH — this entry overrides the framing lines above. There is no subject, no background and no key colour in this image: the material fills the frame edge to edge, fully opaque, and there must be no green pixel anywhere. There is no key light and no shadow — the lighting is flat, even and shadowless, identical in every part of the frame, with no vignette, no falloff, no gradient, no hot spot and no visible light direction. This image is not composited onto the dark slate ground; it IS the dark slate ground.

Seen from directly overhead, perfectly flat on: the bare deck plate of a machine floor. Cold desaturated blue-grey engineered stone — cast mineral aggregate, quarried, poured and ground flat. Surface character at three scales and nothing else: a broad slow cloudiness about one twentieth of the frame across; an even fine granular tooth over the whole surface; and sparse isolated speckles — a few brighter mineral flecks and a few darker pinholes, scattered evenly and never clustered into a shape.

Nothing structural anywhere: no panel lines, no joints, no seams, no tiles, no grid, no bricks, no plates, no rivets, no bolts, no hatches, no drains, no scratches, no scuffs, no tracks, no footprints, no wear paths, no stains, no rust, no dirt, no moss, no vegetation, no water, no cracks, no edges, no border, no frame, and no object of any kind. The renderer draws the panel joints, the tile grid and every luminance step on top of this material; anything here that reads as a line will fight them.

Even coverage is the whole job: any square region of this frame must be interchangeable with any other. Mean tone RGB(40,48,57); every pixel inside the desaturated blue-grey range #1C242B to #4E5E6B, with the darkest and brightest points of the frame no more than one third of that range apart.
prompts.notes: TIER B. Four independent draws of ONE prompt, assembled by the baker into a 2x2 mosaic: -01 top-left, -02 top-right, -03 bottom-left, -04 bottom-right. Crop 2304x2304 from each — an INTERIOR window, never touching the frame edge, which is where the model puts its vignette — reduce 4x (two box-halvings) to 576x576, assemble to 1152x1152 = WorldPxR at RS=4. QUANTIZE ONCE, AFTER ASSEMBLY: four independently median-cut quadrants carry four palettes and the joins appear as colour steps across the middle of the board. Equalize per-quadrant mean and stddev BEFORE quantization if the joins fail. Verification, both mechanical: (a) block flatness — split the assembled 1152x1152 into an 8x8 grid of 144px blocks, assert every block's mean luma is within +/-3 of the field mean (kills vignettes, which are what make a mosaic seam findable); (b) join test — mean |dLuma| across the x=576 column join and the y=576 row join must not exceed 1.25x the mean |dLuma| of interior columns/rows. Consumed by plateAt as `base` in place of BgDark; plateAt keeps its per-tile shade hash, its PanelPeriodPx joints, its flecks and pinholes, and gains the two §3.4 deltas missing today (+3% luminance inside the safe ring; amber-etched Fortress chamber floor). Sample point is the ABSOLUTE world pixel (wx,wy) — this is why the field is full-arena and non-tiling: no two of the 2,040 ground tiles may match.
prompts.comment: Why 4 images when the plan says 1: the plan's own hard crop rule (crop/target == 2^k, k>=2) cannot be met for a 1152x1152 target from any single generation. The smallest legal crop is 4608x4608 and the largest supported frame is 4K = 4096. Quadrants are the minimum-image-count compliant path: 576x576 targets take a 2304x2304 crop (k=2) which fits inside 4096 with room to place the window. Alternatives rejected: one 4K frame reduced by 3.56x (violates the rule, and a non-power-of-two resample is exactly the aliased mush step 5 exists to prevent); a 3x3 mosaic of 2K frames (9 images); baking the field smaller and wrapping it (reintroduces a repeat and a wrap seam at absolute coordinates, destroying the non-tiling property that is the entire reason this asset is full-arena). The seam risk is real but it is a LOW-FREQUENCY risk only, and the prompt is written to remove low-frequency energy entirely: no features, no vignette, no gradient, uniform statistics. A material with no large-scale structure has nothing to mismatch across a join.

prompts.name: wall-face
prompts.prompt:
MATERIAL SWATCH — this entry overrides the framing lines above. There is no subject, no background and no key colour in this image: the material fills the frame edge to edge, fully opaque, and there must be no green pixel anywhere. There is no key light and no shadow — flat, even, shadowless illumination, identical brightness in every part of the frame, no vignette, no gradient, no hot spot, no light direction.

Seen from directly overhead, perfectly flat on: the flat top surface of one monolithic block of dark blue-grey engineered stone — the roof face of a fortress parapet, the material inside the wall and nothing else. Dense fine granular grain, a faint broad cloudiness beneath it, and a light even scatter of small darker inclusions.

This is NOT masonry and must contain no drawn structure of any kind: no bricks, no courses, no block joints, no mortar lines, no seams, no bevels, no chamfers, no rims, no edges, no corners, no highlights, no shadows, no rivets, no bolts, no panel lines, no cracks, no chips, no wear, no lettering. The renderer derives every edge, bevel, roof seam and contact line from the collision mask and paints them over this material; one drawn edge here decouples the art from the geometry and the tile is rejected.

Seamless and tileable in both axes: this frame must repeat against itself with no visible join. Keep the character uniform and fine; keep the brightness identical at all four edges and in the middle; and put no feature, blotch, dark patch or bright patch larger than one sixteenth of the frame anywhere.

Darker and denser than a floor: mean tone near #36444F, every pixel inside #1C242B to #4E5E6B.
prompts.notes: TIER B — the most dangerous asset in the plan (risk #4). Crop 1536x1536 as an INTERIOR window, reduce 4x to 384x384. Consumed ONLY by parapetColorAt's `else: base` branch: the 4-ray openDistDir edge classification stays verbatim, StoneInk contact line at edge<=1, lit/shadowed bevel to WallBevelPx=8, roof seam at (wx+wy) mod RoofSeamPeriod. Fortress reuses the SAME material at shade(+22) — a brighter ramp, not a second image (§3.4). SEAMLESSNESS IS THE BAKER'S JOB, NOT THE MODEL'S: no supported frame size is a 2^k multiple of 384 (1024/384=2.67, 2048/384=5.33, 4096/384=10.67), so the crop is always an interior window and whatever tileability the model produced is cut away. Baker: (1) measure — edgeDelta = mean|L(x=383,y) - L(x=0,y)| over y, and the same for the y axis; interiorDelta = mean|L(x,y) - L(x+1,y)| over the interior; require edgeDelta <= 1.25 * interiorDelta on both axes; (2) if it fails, apply a deterministic wrap-blend over a 32px band (1/12 of the tile) with a cosine window, then re-measure; (3) block flatness — 8x8 grid of 48px blocks, each mean luma within +/-3 of the image mean, which is what keeps the 16-tile repeat undetectable. Order matters: wrap-blend BEFORE median-cut, or the blend invents off-ramp colours that the palette lint then rejects.
prompts.comment: The prompt spends most of its words on what NOT to draw because the failure mode here is not ugliness, it is a flat AI wall tile pasted per-tile: it decouples the art from the colliders and restores exactly the graph-paper look parapetColorAt was written to kill. The material must be featureless BECAUSE the geometry is drawn from the collision mask. Observation for whoever writes the baker: 384 = 16 tiles at RS=4, so the repeat period lands exactly on the tile grid and every 16th tile boundary coincides with the wrap seam — the one place a residual seam would be reinforced rather than hidden. A 512x512 face would wrap every 21.33 tiles (never aligning to the grid) AND could be cropped full-frame at exactly 4x from a 2K generation, preserving any tileability the model actually achieved. The plan says 384; this is flagged, not changed.

prompts.name: rock-cluster-2x2
prompts.prompt:
Seen from directly above and very slightly in front — the board's viewpoint, which overrides the front-view line above — a single compact cluster of angular quarried slate boulders: three to five blocks jammed together and reading as one mass, not as separate stones.

Hard faceted geometry: flat chamfered planes, sharp arrises, blunt broken corners. No rounded pebbles, no smooth erosion, no sand, no rubble scattered outside the mass, and nothing organic — no moss, no lichen, no grass, no soil, no snow, no water.

The cluster completely covers a square footprint and every part of that square is stone: no hole, no gap, no notch, no crevice cut through to the background and no floating separate piece anywhere inside it. Its outline may break the square only within the outermost one twelfth of the footprint, as chipped corners and a chamfered rim.

Lighting is the renderer's one rule: upper-left facets at the bright end of the blue-grey ramp, lower-right facets at the dark end, and a single hard pale-cyan phosphor edge highlight — one line, no wider than one twelfth of the footprint — running along the topmost edges only. No other highlight, no specular sparkle, no rim light on any other side, no glow, no bloom, no haze.

Hard edges against the key colour: the silhouette is a clean cut, with no soft blur, no feathering, no drop shadow, no ambient-occlusion halo and no coloured fringe.

Designed to stay legible when reduced to a 48x48 pixel sprite: bold silhouette, large shapes, no fine detail, no thin lines under 1/12 of the sprite width.

Draw it centred, occupying the middle three quarters of the frame in both axes, with a clean flat key-colour margin one eighth of the frame wide on all four sides.
prompts.notes: TIER A. Crop 1536x1536 centred on the cluster, reduce 32x (five box-halvings) to 48x48 = 2x2 tiles at RS=4. Three draws because clusters should DIFFER (plan §3.3 single-vs-sheet); arena.nim places 10 clusters per seed at PRNG origins, w = 2 or 3 wide, h always 2. Composited into SpBackground at the cluster origin, over the plate. COLLIDER GUARD: tkRock is blocking (isBlocking includes tkWall, tkRock, tkFortressWall), so art that leaves a corner transparent shows open floor the agent cannot walk on. Baker asserts alpha == 255 for every pixel at least 2px inside the 48x48 rect boundary, and fails the bake otherwise. Note arena.nim only converts tiles that were tkGround, so a cluster overlapping the border or the Fortress skirt leaves holes in the rect — the compositor must draw cluster art only where the tile actually is tkRock and fall back to rock-orphan for any tkRock the cluster stamps miss.
prompts.comment: Single, not sheet, and three variants: the three clusters must look like three different piles of the same rock. Cross-variant consistency is carried by the palette and the one-key lighting rule stated identically in all three rock entries, not by co-generation — a sheet here would make the three read as one repeated prop, which is the current build's problem, not its solution.

prompts.name: rock-cluster-3x2
prompts.prompt:
Seen from directly above and very slightly in front — the board's viewpoint, which overrides the front-view line above — a single wide cluster of angular quarried slate boulders: four to six blocks jammed together and reading as one mass, half again as wide as it is tall.

Hard faceted geometry: flat chamfered planes, sharp arrises, blunt broken corners. No rounded pebbles, no smooth erosion, no sand, no rubble scattered outside the mass, and nothing organic — no moss, no lichen, no grass, no soil, no snow, no water.

The cluster completely covers a rectangular footprint three units wide and two units tall, and every part of that rectangle is stone: no hole, no gap, no notch, no crevice cut through to the background and no floating separate piece anywhere inside it. Its outline may break the rectangle only within the outermost one twelfth of the footprint, as chipped corners and a chamfered rim.

Lighting is the renderer's one rule: upper-left facets at the bright end of the blue-grey ramp, lower-right facets at the dark end, and a single hard pale-cyan phosphor edge highlight — one line, no wider than one twelfth of the footprint height — running along the topmost edges only. No other highlight, no specular sparkle, no rim light on any other side, no glow, no bloom, no haze.

Hard edges against the key colour: the silhouette is a clean cut, with no soft blur, no feathering, no drop shadow, no ambient-occlusion halo and no coloured fringe.

Designed to stay legible when reduced to a 72x48 pixel sprite: bold silhouette, large shapes, no fine detail, no thin lines under 1/12 of the sprite height.

Draw it centred, spanning a little more than half the frame's width and a little more than half its height, with a wide clean flat key-colour margin all the way around.
prompts.notes: TIER A. Crop 1152x768 centred on the cluster (both axes reduce 16x — the k on width and height MUST match: 1152/72 = 768/48 = 16), giving 72x48 = 3x2 tiles at RS=4. The 3:2 frame matches the 3:2 footprint, which is why the crop lands at 56.25% of the frame on both axes rather than the 75% used by the square entries — hence 'a little more than half' in the prompt rather than 'the middle three quarters'. Same collider guard as rock-cluster-2x2: alpha == 255 at least 2px inside the 72x48 rect, and the compositor draws only over tiles that are actually tkRock.
prompts.comment: arena.nim: `let w = 2 + rng.rand(2)` (2 or 3 wide) and `let h = 2` always — so 3x2 is three tiles WIDE by two tall, never the transpose. There is no 2x3 asset and there must not be one.

prompts.name: rock-orphan
prompts.prompt:
Seen from directly above and very slightly in front — the board's viewpoint, which overrides the front-view line above — one single angular quarried slate boulder, a broken block filling a square footprint.

Hard faceted geometry: two or three flat chamfered planes meeting at sharp arrises, blunt broken corners. No rounded pebble, no smooth erosion, no sand, no rubble around it, nothing organic — no moss, no lichen, no grass, no soil.

The boulder completely covers its square footprint and every part of that square is stone: no hole, no gap and no notch anywhere inside it. Its outline may break the square only within the outermost one twelfth of the footprint.

Same stone and the same one lighting rule as a cluster of these blocks, so this can sit directly beside one and read as the same material, not a different rock: upper-left facets bright, lower-right facets dark, and a single hard pale-cyan phosphor edge highlight one line wide along the topmost edges only. No other highlight, no sparkle, no glow, no bloom, no haze.

Hard edges against the key colour: clean cut silhouette, no soft blur, no feathering, no drop shadow, no ambient-occlusion halo, no coloured fringe.

Designed to stay legible when reduced to a 24x24 pixel sprite: bold silhouette, large shapes, no fine detail, no thin lines under 1/12 of the sprite width.

Draw it centred, occupying the middle three quarters of the frame in both axes, with a clean flat key-colour margin one eighth of the frame wide on all four sides.
prompts.notes: TIER A. Crop 1536x1536, reduce 64x (six box-halvings) to 24x24 = one tile at RS=4. Covers every tkRock tile the 2x2 / 3x2 cluster stamps do not: arena.nim only converts tiles that were tkGround, so clusters clipped by the border wall, the Fortress skirt or a pedestal leave single orphan tiles behind, and the compositor's fallback must not look like a different quarry. Same collider guard: alpha == 255 at least 2px inside the 24x24 rect.
prompts.comment: One image, not three. This tile is a filler that appears a handful of times per seed and always adjacent to a cluster; variants would draw the eye to exactly the tiles that should disappear into the mass.

prompts.name: pedestal-disarmed
prompts.prompt:
Seen from directly above, perfectly flat on — this is a floor tile, which overrides the front-view line above.

A square amber pad set flush into the floor, filling a square footprint completely, edge to edge, with no background showing anywhere inside it: a broad flat machined top face in warm amber, a chamfered raised rim one sixth of the width running all the way round, a darker recessed groove just inside that rim, and two small bright amber studs sitting on the upper-left diagonal of the top face. Machined resin and metal, not a gem and not a glowing crystal: flat faces, hard edges, no glow, no bloom, no halo, no reflection, no gradient banding, no bevel highlight other than the rim's own chamfer.

This is the disarmed state: the rim is plain amber, calm and inert. No stripes, no chevrons, no hatching, no warning marks, no red of any kind, no symbol, no lettering.

Warm amber only, #3A2610 to #FFD9A0, with the near-black blue #10161C used only for the recessed groove and the outer ink edge.

Designed to stay legible when reduced to a 24x24 pixel sprite: bold silhouette, large shapes, no fine detail, no thin lines under 1/12 of the sprite width.

Draw it centred, occupying the middle three quarters of the frame in both axes, with a clean flat key-colour margin one eighth of the frame wide on all four sides.
prompts.notes: TIER A. Crop 1536x1536, reduce 64x to 24x24. Fully opaque over the whole tile (pedestalAt fills ring + interior today; the floor must not show through). Composited into SpBackground over the plate; selected by tick >= 240. Costs exactly one extra background define at t=240 when the arena swaps armed -> disarmed.
prompts.comment: Two singles rather than a 2-cell sheet, per plan §3.3 ('single where variants should differ: ... the pedestal states'). The pad description is held WORD-FOR-WORD identical between pedestal-disarmed and pedestal-armed so the only textual difference is the stripe ring — that is what carries consistency across two separate calls. Pre-computed fallback if the two pads still read as different objects at 1:1 on the poster: replace both entries with one 2-cell sheet at 3:2 @ 2K, cells 1024x1365, crop 768x768 centred in each cell (k=5, 32x -> 24x24). The swap is then mechanical.

prompts.name: pedestal-armed
prompts.prompt:
Seen from directly above, perfectly flat on — this is a floor tile, which overrides the front-view line above.

A square amber pad set flush into the floor, filling a square footprint completely, edge to edge, with no background showing anywhere inside it: a broad flat machined top face in warm amber, a chamfered raised rim one sixth of the width running all the way round, a darker recessed groove just inside that rim, and two small bright amber studs sitting on the upper-left diagonal of the top face. Machined resin and metal, not a gem and not a glowing crystal: flat faces, hard edges, no glow, no bloom, no halo, no reflection, no gradient banding, no bevel highlight other than the rim's own chamfer.

This is the armed state, and the only difference is the rim: the chamfered rim — and nothing else in the image — carries a bold hazard stripe, alternating 45-degree bars of warm amber and near-black blue running continuously all the way round, each bar at least one twelfth of the footprint wide. The top face inside the rim is unchanged and must stay a clear plain amber field. No red anywhere, no warning triangle, no exclamation mark, no symbol, no lettering, no glow.

Warm amber only, #3A2610 to #FFD9A0, with the near-black blue #10161C used only for the hazard bars, the recessed groove and the outer ink edge.

Designed to stay legible when reduced to a 24x24 pixel sprite: bold silhouette, large shapes, no fine detail, no thin lines under 1/12 of the sprite width.

Draw it centred, occupying the middle three quarters of the frame in both axes, with a clean flat key-colour margin one eighth of the frame wide on all four sides.
prompts.notes: TIER A. Crop 1536x1536, reduce 64x to 24x24. Fully opaque over the whole tile. Selected by tick < 240 — VISUAL_REDESIGN §3.4's pre-ignition mine state, which is missing from the build entirely today. The Klaxon-red corner ticks §3.4 asks for during the countdown are STAMPED IN CODE over this sprite, not generated (see comment).
prompts.comment: No red in the generation, deliberately. Risk #8 and §3.1: semantic colours (Klaxon #FF4A36, Directive Magenta, team hue) appear only as LINES AND GLYPHS THE CODE DRAWS — fills vs lines is itself an information channel. Generated art is team-neutral and semantic-neutral: Etch / Phosphor / Amber only. Baking red into the armed pedestal would put a semantic colour into a fill permanently and would also freeze the countdown's most dramatic beat into a static texture. The hazard stripe is amber-on-ink, which is legal ramp material; the red corner ticks stay a 12-line code stamp that can pulse on the countdown cadence.

prompts.name: bush-clump
prompts.prompt:
Seen from directly above and slightly in front — the board's viewpoint, which overrides the front-view line above — a small dense clump of dead angular scrub. This is the only organic thing in a machine world and it has been drawn as if it were mineral: a tight bundle of hard chipped shards and stiff broken twigs, not soft foliage.

Desaturated blue-grey at the dark end of the ramp, #1C242B to #3E4D59 only. There is no green in this image and no plant colour of any kind — not olive, not sage, not grey-green, not brown, not straw. A lighter crown catching the key light along the top, a darker underside, and a frayed irregular rim that breaks into a few separate shards at the edge. At most one hard pale-cyan phosphor edge line along the very top of the crown, no wider than one twelfth of the sprite.

No berries, no fruit, no seeds, no buds, no flowers, no round spots of any kind, and no bright dots anywhere. A countable pip is gameplay state and is stamped separately; anything round and light in this drawing would be counted as a charge that does not exist.

The clump sits inside its square footprint without filling the corners — it is a free silhouette, not a tile, and open floor must show around it. Hard edges against the key colour: clean cut silhouette, no soft blur, no feathering, no glow, no bloom, no haze, no drop shadow.

Designed to stay legible when reduced to a 24x24 pixel sprite: bold silhouette, large shapes, no fine detail, no thin lines under 1/12 of the sprite width.

Draw it centred, occupying the middle three quarters of the frame in both axes, with a clean flat key-colour margin one eighth of the frame wide on all four sides.
prompts.notes: TIER A. Crop 1536x1536, reduce 64x to 24x24. ONE image emits four sprites (SpBushBase 90..93): code composites 0-3 amber pips on top at fixed spots. Note the deliberate contrast with the rock entries: rocks MUST fill their footprint opaquely because tkRock is a collider; bushes MUST NOT, because a bush is an entity on LayerMap with charges, blocks nothing, and reads better with floor visible around it. Phase 0 prerequisite: SpBushBase 90..93 currently collides with SpProjBase + ord(iArrows|iDarts) = 91,92 in the same spriteDefs packet — last define wins, so two of the three bush charge states render as an 8x8 projectile blob today. Move SpProjBase to 960 before this art means anything.
prompts.comment: The most clear-cut art-bible violation in the codebase is here: bushPixels' leaf is (46,108,50) and its berries are (215,45,60) — §3.1 says 'there is no green anywhere in the identity — nothing in this game means go'. Phase 2 converts those to Etch-dark + amber pips BEFORE this asset is generated, because baked art freezes its palette. The prompt bans round bright shapes twice, in two different words, because a generated berry is not a cosmetic error: charges are countable gameplay state and a baked-in pip is a permanent lie about how many the bush has.

prompts.name: chip-body
prompts.prompt:
Seen from directly above, perfectly flat on — this is a token lying on the floor, which overrides the front-view line above.

A single machined amber token shaped as a diamond — a square rotated 45 degrees — with its four points reaching almost to the four edges of the footprint. A hard bevelled edge all the way round; one broad flat upper-left facet catching the key light; one darker lower-right facet in shadow; a crisp near-black blue rim line about one twelfth of the width; and a single small bright square specular mark high on the upper-left facet.

Machined resin and metal, not a gemstone: flat facets, hard edges, no sparkle, no refraction, no caustics, no glow, no bloom, no halo, no gradient banding, no inner pattern, no chamfer detail beyond the single main bevel.

Warm amber only, #3A2610 to #FFD9A0, with the near-black blue #10161C used only for the rim line.

The centre must stay a broad, plain, uncluttered field: a separate contents mark is composited on top of it, so put no detail, no marking, no logo, no ridge, no hole, no groove and no highlight anywhere inside the middle three fifths of the diamond.

Hard edges against the key colour: clean cut silhouette, no soft blur, no feathering, no drop shadow, no haze.

Designed to stay legible when reduced to a 24x24 pixel sprite: bold silhouette, large shapes, no fine detail, no thin lines under 1/12 of the sprite width.

Draw it centred, occupying the middle three quarters of the frame in both axes, with a clean flat key-colour margin one eighth of the frame wide on all four sides.
prompts.notes: TIER A. Crop 1536x1536, reduce 64x to 24x24. ONE chip body shared by all twelve items: with itemColor collapsed to a single amber ramp in Phase 2, hue can no longer carry identity and the stencil must. Emits 12 ground-chip sprites (SpItemBase 51..62) as chip + stencil[i]. The 'middle three fifths' clear zone is sized against the stencil geometry: a mark spanning 14 of 24 final px fits inside the diamond's inscribed square (~17px) with margin. itemPixels keeps its amber addBacklight so matter still separates from the plate.
prompts.comment: Single image, no variants. This is the plan's whole economic argument in one asset: 12 chips that differed only by tint become 1 body + 12 marks, and identity moves from a channel the palette forbids (hue) to one it encodes (shape). itemColor is not art — it is a 13-entry lookup table and the most consequential entry in the catalogue; collapsing it is the PREREQUISITE for this asset, not a consequence of it.

prompts.name: crate-body
prompts.prompt:
Seen from directly above and slightly in front — the board's viewpoint, which overrides the front-view line above — a small chamfered supply crate filling a square footprint.

A broad flat lit top face; four short bevelled side walls falling away below it and to the right; all four corners cut off by deep 45-degree chamfers; a recessed strap band crossing the lower third from side to side; and one small machined seal square in the upper-left corner. Warm amber only, #3A2610 to #FFD9A0, with the near-black blue #10161C for the recessed band, the corner seal and the outer ink edge.

Printed by a machine, not built by hand: no planks, no wood grain, no knots, no nails, no screws, no hinges, no handles, no rope, no webbing, no buckles, no parachute, no canopy, no cord, no antenna, no light, no lettering, no icon, no logo, no barcode.

It must read correctly while it is being revealed one row at a time from the top down, because the machine prints it row by row. Keep the composition horizontally banded and continuous from top to bottom; put nothing in it that only makes sense once the bottom row exists — no legs, no ground shadow, no floating element, no detail hanging below the body, nothing tapering to a point at the very bottom.

The middle of the top face must stay a broad, plain, uncluttered field: a contents mark is composited there, so put no detail, no marking and no highlight anywhere inside the middle three fifths of the footprint.

Hard edges against the key colour: clean cut silhouette, no soft blur, no feathering, no drop shadow, no glow, no bloom, no haze.

Designed to stay legible when reduced to a 24x24 pixel sprite: bold silhouette, large shapes, no fine detail, no thin lines under 1/12 of the sprite width.

Draw it centred, occupying the middle three quarters of the frame in both axes, with a clean flat key-colour margin one eighth of the frame wide on all four sides.
prompts.notes: TIER A. Crop 1536x1536, reduce 64x to 24x24. Emits 12 landed-crate sprites (SpCrateBase 901..912) as crate + stencil[i], PLUS the 6 print frames: cratePartPixels(n) becomes a row-slice of this same baked crate with the amber print-head line drawn at the cut, which removes the touchdown pop for free (today the print frames and the landed crate are two different drawings). The row-slice requirement is why the prompt bans anything that only resolves at the bottom row. Phase 2 must land first: crate wood (150,105,55) -> chamfered amber, and the mid-height contents band moves to the lower third so the stencil zone is clear.
prompts.comment: One body, 12 stencils, one glyph vocabulary — and the vocabulary is the SAME one used on the chips, so a player learns each mark once and then reads it on ground loot, on a landed pod and (tinted phosphor) in an agent's hand. This is what fixes the anonymous-crate problem: today every pod looks identical until it is opened.

prompts.name: stencil-sheet
prompts.prompt:
A 4-column by 3-row grid of twelve flat abstract stencil marks, one mark centred in each cell, the twelve cells filling the frame edge to edge in a regular grid. Every cell is plain flat #00FF00 carrying a single solid mark drawn in near-black blue #10161C and nothing else — no cell borders, no frame, no grid lines, no dividing rules, no numbers, no captions, no drop shadows.

These are masks, not pictures: each mark is one flat solid silhouette in a single colour, with no shading, no gradient, no outline, no highlight, no perspective, no depth and no interior detail except holes cut clean through.

Reading left to right, top to bottom:
Row 1 — (1) SWORD: a broad straight blade standing vertically, point up, with a wide straight crossguard low down and a short grip below it. (2) SPEAR: a long thin shaft lying on the diagonal from lower-left to upper-right, with one large solid triangular head at the upper end and no crossguard. (3) BOW: a tall C-shaped arc opening to the right, with a straight vertical string joining its two tips. (4) KNIVES: two short broad tapered blades crossed in an X, points outward.
Row 2 — (5) BLOWGUN: one long straight horizontal tube with a flared conical mouthpiece at the left end and a small notch at the right end. (6) NET: a square patch of coarse diamond mesh — thick bars crossing on both diagonals — with four heavier round weights at its corners. (7) FIRST AID: a thick equal-armed cross centred inside a rounded square outline. (8) RATIONS: a squat rounded tin standing upright, with a raised lid line across its top quarter and a small tab on the lid.
Row 3 — (9) BACKPACK: an upright rounded bag with two shoulder-strap arcs rising from its top edge and one horizontal flap line across its upper third. (10) CAMOUFLAGE: three overlapping irregular rounded blobs of different sizes, like a camouflage patch, touching but not concentric. (11) ARROWS: two long parallel shafts on the diagonal pointing up and to the right, each with a solid chevron head and a pair of straight fletching bars at the tail. (12) DARTS: three short stubby needles fanned from a common point at the lower left, pointing up and to the right, each with a round bulb at its tail — clearly shorter and fatter than the arrows.

All twelve must belong to one family: the same stroke weight, the same optical weight, the same blunt machined terminals, everything built from thick bars, wedges and discs. No mark may have a stroke thinner than one twelfth of its own width. Each mark is centred in its cell and spans a little under half the cell's width. Nothing touches a cell edge and nothing overlaps a neighbouring cell.
prompts.notes: TIER A. 4:3 @ 2K -> nominal cells 512x512; crop 384x384 centred in each cell (nominal origin 512c+64, 512r+64), reduce 16x to 24x24. HAND-VERIFY every rect against actual_px before writing art/sheets.json — the model does not grid reliably and a mis-crop is silent. Cell order is ord(ItemId) 1..12: sword, spear, bow, knives, blowgun, net, first_aid, rations, backpack, camouflage, arrows, darts (iNone = 0 is a transparent 13th entry the baker synthesizes, never generated). Baked as a MASK: keep the alpha, let code choose the tint — ink over the amber chip and the amber crate, pale-cyan phosphor over the carrier's hand point. Emits 24 sprites (12 chips + 12 crates) from this one call, and up to 6 more (SpWeaponBase 601..606) if the held glyphs are cut here as a CONCENTRIC 320x320 crop of cells 1-6 (same centre as the 384x384 rect, k=4, 16x -> 20x20) instead of being generated separately — see the cross-group note in the file header. A mark reduces to ~14 of the 24 final px, which fits inside the chip diamond's inscribed square with margin.
prompts.comment: ONE SHEET, not twelve calls — decided, with the trade-off stated. For: the twelve marks are a VOCABULARY, and stroke weight, terminal shape, mark density and optical size have to agree across all twelve or the eye reads 'twelve different families' instead of 'twelve different items'; only co-generation conditions each mark on its siblings. Drift between twelve separate calls is invisible when you inspect one mark and glaring on a board with eight chips down. It is also one request, one cache key, one hand-verification pass. Against: a mis-crop is silent, and one bad cell means re-billing all twelve. Escape hatch, deliberately NOT added as dead entries here (generate.py runs every entry in the group, so twelve unused entries would bill twelve calls on the next run): if exactly one mark fails review, add a temporary single entry named stencil-single-<item> at 1:1 @ 2K with that one mark's sentence verbatim, framed 'centred, spanning a little under half the frame width', crop 1536x1536 -> 24x24 (k=6), then delete the entry once art/sheets.json points at the replacement PNG. Hardest confusion set is knives / arrows / darts — three groups of sharp things — so they are separated by TOPOLOGY, not by detail: crossed vs parallel vs fanned, long vs long vs short, no tail vs fletching vs bulb. Sword / spear / blowgun are separated by AXIS: vertical vs diagonal vs horizontal, which is the only difference that survives a 16x reduction.

prompts.name: stencil-sheet-b
prompts.notes: SUPPLEMENT (2026-08-18): the main stencil-sheet generation came out 3x3 with nine marks; these are the four the vocabulary still needs. 2x2 grid, same crop discipline: detect each cell's mark bbox, centre a square crop, reduce to 24x24. Same family rules as stencil-sheet.
prompts.prompt:
A 2 column by 2 row grid of four flat pictogram marks, one mark centred in each of four equal square cells, the marks separated by the flat background alone — no gutter lines, no borders, no boxes, no captions.

Reading order, and it must be exactly this:
  top left     — a bow: one vertical arc with a straight vertical string, curve opening to the left
  top right    — a camouflage cloak: a hooded poncho silhouette, wide at the hem, narrowing to the hood
  bottom left  — three arrows in a vertical bundle, points up, fletching visible at the base
  bottom right — three short darts in a vertical bundle, points up, clearly shorter and slighter than arrows

Every mark is a single flat fill of near-black #10161C and nothing else: flat silhouettes with hard edges, every stroke straight — horizontal, vertical or at 45 degrees, corners cut square. All four marks share one weight and one scale, each filling about two thirds of its cell. The background is one continuous field of pure #00FF00 touching all four edges.

prompts.name: burst-star
prompts.prompt:
A single radial burst seen flat on, centred on flat pure #00FF00. Draw it as a flat monochrome mask in one solid near-black blue #10161C, with no shading, no gradient, no colour variation and no soft edge anywhere — only its silhouette survives, and the renderer tints and fades it.

Eight straight tapering rays radiate from a small solid core: one up, one down, one left, one right and one along each diagonal, each ray widest where it meets the core and narrowing to a blunt tip, all eight the same length and thickness, so the figure is symmetric about both axes and both diagonals. The core is a solid disc about one sixth of the star's diameter.

Between the rays, a scatter of small separate specks — hard-edged squares and stubby wedges, not dots of light — dense near the core and thinning outward, so the outer part of the figure breaks into particles instead of ending cleanly. The scatter is irregular; the rays are not.

No smoke, no fire, no flame, no embers with trails, no lens flare, no glow, no bloom, no halo, no motion blur, no soft falloff, no vignette: every edge is a hard cut and nothing is drawn at partial opacity.

Designed to stay legible when reduced to a 72x72 pixel sprite and again to 48x48: no ray narrower than one twentieth of the star's diameter at its base, and no separate speck smaller than one thirty-sixth of the star's diameter.

Draw it centred, spanning a little more than half the frame's width, with a wide clean flat key-colour margin all the way around.
prompts.notes: TIER A. Crop 1152x1152 centred, reduce 16x to 72x72. ONE image emits 15 sprites: 3 tints (Bone #E9E4D8 / Amber #FFB454 / Klaxon #FF4A36) x 5 fade stages via dimmed(), with the pedestal-mine burst scaled to 48x48. Fires on Part 7's pivotal beats: death peak-white, mine ignition (1-frame white + red cross-flash), Fortress ignition starburst. THE ALPHA DISCIPLINE MATTERS MOST HERE (risk #2): dimmed() scales alpha proportionally, so any residual haze in the empty corners survives every fade stage as a dim floating rectangle over the board — the one failure dimmed() cannot rescue. Baker: a < 24 -> bitwise (0,0,0,0), then assert the alpha histogram has zero mass in 1..23 and the transparent region is exactly zero. The speck floor (1/36 of the diameter) is the reduction arithmetic made explicit: 1152/36 = 32 source px = 2 px at 72, which is the smallest speck that survives a 16x area reduction with alpha above the 24 cutoff. WARNING: FadeStages cannot be raised without re-spacing sprite ids 920/924/928/932 — they are packed exactly FadeStages apart and will silently overlap.
prompts.comment: Monochrome mask rather than coloured art, matching the plan's own pattern, because the burst is the one asset that must be three different semantic colours: Bone, Amber and Klaxon are LINE/GLYPH colours the code owns (§3.1, risk #8), and baking any of them into the source would both violate the fills-vs-lines channel and triple the image count. Symmetric rays plus irregular scatter is the deliberate split from VISUAL_REDESIGN §3.3's two opposed laws: the vector starburst reads as a diagram (the machine emitting), the broken tips read as thrown particles (matter being freed).
